name: CEM
tagline: Cross-Entropy Method: refit a Gaussian to the top-K elite trajectories each iteration; return the final mean.
pseudocode:
1. Init $\mu \leftarrow 0$, $\sigma \leftarrow 1.5$ (per timestep).
2. For iter $1\ldots N$:
3. \quad Sample $A \sim \mathcal N(\mu,\sigma^2)$, $B$ trajectories of length $H$.
4. \quad Clip per-step action norm to 2.45.
5. \quad Score with $J(A) = \text{cost}(A; \hat o_0)$ via JEPA rollout.
6. \quad Pick top-$K$ elites ($K = \max(10, B/10)$).
7. \quad $\mu \leftarrow \text{mean}(A_{\text{elite}}),\; \sigma \leftarrow \text{std}(A_{\text{elite}})$.
8. Return $\mu$ as the planned action sequence.
diff_from_baseline: Rubinstein 1997 / Botev et al. 2013 — standard model-based-planning baseline. Refits a per-timestep Gaussian to elite returns under a learned (here JEPA) dynamics model.

name: MPPI
tagline: Sampling-based path-integral control: softmax-weighted update of the action distribution by exp(temperature * cost).
pseudocode:
1. Init $\mu\!\leftarrow\!0$, $\sigma\!\leftarrow\!2$.
2. For iter $1\ldots N$:
3. \quad Sample $A^{(b)}\!\sim\!\mathcal N(\mu,\sigma^2)$, score $J^{(b)}$ via JEPA rollout.
4. \quad Take top-$K$ elites; let $J_{\min}\!=\!\min_b J^{(b)}$.
5. \quad $w^{(k)} \propto \exp\!\bigl(\lambda(J_{\min}-J^{(k)})\bigr)$ over the $K$ elites.
6. \quad $\mu \leftarrow \sum_k w^{(k)} A^{(k)},\; \sigma^2 \leftarrow \sum_k w^{(k)}(A^{(k)}-\mu)^2$.
7. Sample one elite by $w$ as the executed action sequence.
diff_from_baseline: Williams et al., 'Model Predictive Path Integral Control' (2017). Same sampling skeleton as CEM but uses a soft (exponential-weight) update instead of refitting to a hard top-K elite cut.

name: Random shooting
tagline: Single-pass random sampling of action sequences; pick the lowest-cost rollout. No iterative refinement.
pseudocode:
1. Sample $B$ action sequences $A^{(b)}\!\sim\!\mathcal N(0,1)^{H\times d_a}$.
2. Clip per-step norm to 2.45.
3. Score $J^{(b)}\!=\!\text{cost}(A^{(b)}; \hat o_0)$ via JEPA rollout.
4. Return $A^{(\arg\min J)}$.
diff_from_baseline: Classic random-shooting MPC lower-bound. Useful as a sanity check for any iterative planner that should beat single-pass sampling under the same compute.

name: iCEM
tagline: Improved CEM with colored 1/f^beta noise, sample decay per iteration, elite reuse, momentum, and across-step shift.
pseudocode:
1. On $t_0$: reset $\mu,\sigma$ to (0, 1.5); else shift $\mu$ left by 1, repeat last step, reset $\sigma\!=\!\sigma_{\text{init}}$.
2. For iter $i=1\ldots N$ ($N{=}10$):
3. \quad Sample with colored noise: $\epsilon\!\sim\!1/f^{\,\beta}$ Gaussian (FFT); $A=\mu + \sigma\,\epsilon$.
4. \quad Reuse 30% top elites from prev iter / prev step.
5. \quad Score $J$, take $K{=}10\%$ elites; track best-ever ($A^{\star},J^{\star}$).
6. \quad Momentum update: $\mu \leftarrow 0.9\,\mu_{\text{new}}+0.1\,\mu$ (and $\sigma$).
7. \quad Decay: $B \leftarrow \max(2K,\, B/\gamma)$ with $\gamma{=}1.25$.
8. Return $A^{\star}$ (or final $\mu$ if $J(\mu){<}J^{\star}$).
diff_from_baseline: Pinneri et al., 'Sample-efficient Cross-Entropy Method for Real-time Planning' (CoRL 2020 / PMLR 2021). Adds correlated colored noise, elite reuse, momentum, sample decay, and across-step shift (Sec. 3.2) to vanilla CEM.
